CoordinateSystem3M.capacity: FEEL orientation as embodied direction by standing inside the coordinate frame
CoordinateSystem3M.description: Stand inside the coordinate system. Three meter-long axes — X red, Y green, Z blue — establish the right-handed frame that every 3D operation assumes. A gyroscope gadget shows your orientation relative to the axes. The arbitrary nature of axis conventions becomes visible: right-handed vs left-handed, Y-up vs Z-up are choices, not laws.
CoordinateSystem3M.name: CoordinateSystem3M
CoordinateSystem3M.qfep_connection: Pure F — the coordinate system is the most fundamental structure, the frame from which all measurement begins. Without agreed axes, no vector has components, no transform has a matrix.

ForceMagnitudeDemo.capacity: FEEL that force and acceleration are the same shape by dragging an arrow and watching the ball respond proportionally
ForceMagnitudeDemo.description: Drag the force arrow longer and the ball accelerates harder. F = ma made visceral — magnitude is felt, not read. The ball's trajectory traces the force's history. Reset with R, freeze with Space. Contrasts with WorkEnergyDemo (same force, different measure); feeds into CombinedForcesDemo (multiple forces).
interactions: drag force arrow to change magnitude and direction
ForceMagnitudeDemo.name: ForceMagnitudeDemo
ForceMagnitudeDemo.qfep_connection: Classical F — force as deterministic law. Drag the arrow, the ball obeys. No randomness, no emergence. Pure Newtonian causality where every input produces a proportional output.

VectorAddition.capacity: SEE that the ball knows only the sum of all forces, not the individual forces themselves
VectorAddition.description: Two force arrows, one ball, one truth: nature does not apply forces one at a time. Drag F1 and F2 independently — the yellow net force arrow updates as their vector sum, and the ball accelerates along it. Cancellation when forces oppose. Diagonal trajectories from perpendicular forces. Superposition as felt experience.
VectorAddition.name: VectorAddition
VectorAddition.qfep_connection: F-composition — two deterministic forces combine into one deterministic result. Superposition is linearity made visible. The net force IS the sum, no approximation, no loss.

vector_addition_xl.capacity: WALK between two force arrows and feel their sum reach across the room as the green diagonal of an invisible parallelogram
vector_addition_xl.description: The walk-inside vector addition exhibit. Two grabbable vectors fan out from a shared origin at ~5x5 m so you stand among them; a magnitude slider stretches |a| while a large live readout shows the sum components and length. Drag either tip and the green sum vector and dotted parallelogram update in real time.
interactions: grab and drag either vector tip
vector_addition_xl.name: Vector Addition (Walk-Inside)
vector_addition_xl.qfep_connection: F-composition at body scale — superposition becomes a place you stand inside rather than a diagram you read.

VectorBasics.capacity: UNDERSTAND that a vector is not a number and not a point — it is a displacement carrying both how far and which way
VectorBasics.description: Grab an arrow and stretch it. Watch magnitude, unit vector, and components all update as one system. v = |v| * v-hat — a vector is magnitude times direction, decomposed into (x,y,z) components along the axes. The magnitude arc sweeps from the x-axis. The spring scale responds to vector length like a physical instrument.
VectorBasics.name: VectorBasics
VectorBasics.qfep_connection: Pure F-decomposition — breaking a single quantity into orthogonal components. The vector IS its components, and the components ARE the vector. No information lost, no approximation.

VectorCrossProduct.capacity: FEEL that torque is not a force but the force's opinion about rotation, measured by how far off-center and how perpendicular it acts
VectorCrossProduct.description: Drag the force and its application point. The purple torque vector pops out perpendicular to both, spinning the ball via the right-hand rule. tau = r x F — the cross product. Zero torque when force passes through center (r parallel to F). Maximum torque when perpendicular to the lever arm.
VectorCrossProduct.gamwell_reference: Linear algebra fundamentals, cross product, angular momentum
VectorCrossProduct.name: VectorCrossProduct
VectorCrossProduct.qfep_connection: F-perpendicularity — the cross product extracts the component of interaction that is orthogonal to both inputs. It measures not agreement (that is dot product) but the capacity for rotation.

vector_cross_product_xl.capacity: WALK around two arrows and watch the cross product pop straight up perpendicular to both, its length the area of the parallelogram you stand on
vector_cross_product_xl.description: The walk-inside cross product exhibit at ~5x5 m. Two grabbable vectors span a glowing parallelogram; the purple a x b vector rises perpendicular to both. A magnitude slider stretches |b| and a large live readout shows |a x b| and confirms perpendicularity. The paddle wheel spins by the right-hand rule.
interactions: grab and drag either vector tip
read the live |a x b| readout
vector_cross_product_xl.name: Cross Product (Walk-Inside)
vector_cross_product_xl.qfep_connection: F-perpendicularity at body scale — the orthogonal axis of rotation becomes a thing you can stand beneath.

VectorDotProduct.capacity: SEE that pushing sideways does nothing — work is the component of force that agrees with motion
VectorDotProduct.description: Push a ball and watch the work meter tick up. Push perpendicular and it stays at zero. W = F . d = |F||d|cos(theta) — the dot product made visceral. The meter turns green for positive work, red for negative, yellow for zero. Total work accumulates as a running dot-product integrator over the path.
VectorDotProduct.gamwell_reference: Linear algebra fundamentals, dot product, work-energy theorem
interactions: press R to reset total work
VectorDotProduct.name: VectorDotProduct
VectorDotProduct.qfep_connection: F-projection — the dot product extracts the component of one vector that agrees with another. It measures alignment. Perpendicular forces do zero work because they have zero agreement with the direction of motion.

vector_dot_product_xl.capacity: STAND between two arrows and watch the dot value swing from full agreement to zero as the angle between them opens to a right angle
vector_dot_product_xl.description: The walk-inside dot product exhibit at ~5x5 m. Two grabbable vectors share an origin; the green projection and pink rejection split a along b. A magnitude slider stretches |b| and a large live readout shows a . b and the angle between. The hinge gadget makes the angle physical.
interactions: grab and drag either vector tip
read the live dot + angle readout
vector_dot_product_xl.name: Dot Product (Walk-Inside)
vector_dot_product_xl.qfep_connection: F-projection at body scale — alignment becomes an angle you walk into, and zero work is a right angle you can feel.

VectorFieldFlow.description: F(p) = swirl(p) - radial(p). A vector field assigns a direction to every point. The particle reads the field and follows.
VectorFieldFlow.name: VectorFieldFlow

vector_projection_reflection_xl.capacity: WALK onto the plane and watch an incident arrow split into the part that lies flat and the part that bounces back across the normal
vector_projection_reflection_xl.description: The walk-inside projection and reflection exhibit at ~5x5 m. A grabbable incident vector decomposes against a glowing plane into its in-plane projection and its reflection. Grab the normal to tilt the plane. A magnitude slider stretches the incident vector and a large live readout shows the projection length and the reflected vector.
interactions: grab and drag the incident or normal tip
read the live projection + reflection readout
vector_projection_reflection_xl.name: Projection & Reflection (Walk-Inside)
vector_projection_reflection_xl.qfep_connection: F-decomposition at body scale — the plane and its normal become a floor you stand on and an axis you bounce across.

vector_addition_xl_laser.capacity: Stand inside a 4 m+ vector-addition exhibit and move the arrow tips with the VR laser pointer — point, hold trigger, sweep, and the green sum diagonal follows across the room
vector_addition_xl_laser.description: The walk-inside vector addition exhibit, sized so the tips are out of arm's reach and grabbed with the laser pointer instead. Point either hand's laser at a glowing endpoint (it highlights green), hold the trigger, and sweep to move it; the sum vector and dotted parallelogram update live.
interactions: point the laser at a vector tip and hold the trigger
sweep the laser to move the tip; walk to change depth
vector_addition_xl_laser.name: Vector Addition (Laser, 4 m+)
vector_addition_xl_laser.qfep_connection: F-composition at room scale, reached by light — pointing becomes touching, and superposition is a place you stand inside.

vector_subtraction_xl_laser.capacity: Stand inside a 4 m+ vector-subtraction exhibit and move the arrow tips with the VR laser pointer — watch a − b appear as the arrow from b's tip to a's tip
vector_subtraction_xl_laser.description: The walk-inside vector subtraction exhibit, sized so the tips are out of arm's reach and grabbed with the laser pointer. Point a hand's laser at a glowing endpoint (it highlights green), hold the trigger, and sweep to move it; the difference vector, -b, and the tip-to-tail construction update live.
interactions: point the laser at a vector tip and hold the trigger
sweep the laser to move the tip; walk to change depth
vector_subtraction_xl_laser.name: Vector Subtraction (Laser, 4 m+)
vector_subtraction_xl_laser.qfep_connection: Subtraction as displacement between tips, reached by light — the negative vector made walkable.

VectorThrowing.description: p(t) = p0 + v0*t + 0.5*g*t^2. Projectile motion. Horizontal = constant velocity; vertical = constant acceleration. Your hand writes the initial conditions.
VectorThrowing.name: VectorThrowing

VectorWorkbench.description: Universal vector sandbox - two draggable vectors with all operations (add, subtract, dot, cross, projection) computed live
VectorWorkbench.name: Vector Workbench
VectorWorkbench.qfep_connection: All vector operations in one frame of reference. See relationships between operations. Synthesis of mathematical tools.

ball_dropper.description: Drops colorful physics balls one at a time. Pair with laser_turret for targeting demo. Balls cycle through colors and have configurable physics properties.
ball_dropper.name: Ball Dropper
ball_dropper.qfep_connection: Entropy source - introducing moving targets into the system for the turret to track.

basis_vectors_rig.description: Interactive basis vectors (î, ĵ, k̂) showing how any 3D point is a linear combination: P = xî + yĵ + zk̂.
basis_vectors_rig.name: Basis Vectors Rig

parameters.target_point: Point to decompose into basis components

basis_vectors_rig.qfep_connection: Basis as frame of reference - the coordinate system from which we measure all positions

coordinate_system_switcher.description: Shows the same 3D point in Cartesian (x,y,z), Cylindrical (r,θ,z), and Spherical (ρ,θ,φ) coordinates simultaneously. ImmediateMesh axes and arcs with projection lines showing how each system maps. Color-coded: Cartesian=RGB, Cylindrical=yellow, Spherical=magenta.
coordinate_system_switcher.name: Coordinate System Switcher
coordinate_system_switcher.qfep_connection: Multiple coordinate systems as multiple perspectives on the same reality — the point doesn't change, only the language describing it.

cross_product_demo.description: Interactive cross product: A × B produces a vector perpendicular to both. Shows parallelogram area and right-hand rule.
cross_product_demo.name: Cross Product Demo
cross_product_demo.qfep_connection: Cross product as emergence - a third direction arising from two, perpendicularity as difference

destructibles_test_scene.description: impact → destroy(method). Eight destruction methods: instant, health-based, face-peel, Cantor recursion, Voronoi fracture, planar crack, prism shatter. Topology of breaking.
destructibles_test_scene.name: destructibles_test_scene

dot_product_projector.description: Interactive dot product visualizer showing A · B = |A||B|cos(θ). Demonstrates projection and alignment measurement.
dot_product_projector.name: Dot Product Projector
dot_product_projector.qfep_connection: Dot product as alignment - measuring how much two directions agree or oppose

example_1_1_bouncing_ball_with_no_vector.description: Bouncing ball demonstration without vector math
example_1_1_bouncing_ball_with_no_vector.name: Bouncing Ball with No Vectors VR

example_1_2_bouncing_ball_with_vectors_v.description: Bouncing ball demonstration using vector math
example_1_2_bouncing_ball_with_vectors_v.name: Bouncing Ball with Vectors VR

example_1_8_motion_101_velocity_and_cons.name: Motion 101 Velocity and Constant Acceleration VR

example_1_9_motion_101_velocity_and_rand.name: Motion 101 Velocity and Random Acceleration VR

exercise_1_3_solution_3_d_bouncing_ball_.capacity: WATCH a bouncing ball as a clock that runs down — each bounce measures how much the universe forgot
exercise_1_3_solution_3_d_bouncing_ball_.description: A ball trapped in a box, slowly dying. Position accumulates velocity, velocity accumulates gravity, walls reverse and damp. Each bounce lower than the last as elasticity drains energy. A trail draws the ball's parabolic history as a fading line. The simplest dynamics: one force, one constraint, and the slow settling as the universe forgets.
exercise_1_3_solution_3_d_bouncing_ball_.gamwell_reference: Classical mechanics, Newtonian dynamics, Nature of Code
interactions: see energy decay through diminishing heights
exercise_1_3_solution_3_d_bouncing_ball_.name: 3D Bouncing Ball
exercise_1_3_solution_3_d_bouncing_ball_.qfep_connection: Pure F with dissipation — gravity is constant F, the wall's elasticity coefficient IS lambda. At e=1.0 energy is conserved forever. Below 1.0, each bounce leaks energy into the wall. Lambda controls how fast the system forgets its initial conditions.

exercise_1_5_solution_accelerate_and_dec.capacity: SEE that smooth deceleration emerges from scaling desired speed by distance — arrival is a feedback loop, not a decision
exercise_1_5_solution_accelerate_and_dec.description: A ball chases a moving target, steering with arrival behavior — accelerating toward the target and decelerating as it approaches. The target traces sinusoidal curves through 3D space. When far, the ball applies maximum force. When close, force scales down proportionally, producing smooth deceleration. Seek behavior with distance-based speed ramping.
exercise_1_5_solution_accelerate_and_dec.gamwell_reference: Classical mechanics, Newtonian dynamics, Nature of Code
interactions: observe acceleration phase vs deceleration phase
exercise_1_5_solution_accelerate_and_dec.name: Accelerate and Decelerate
exercise_1_5_solution_accelerate_and_dec.qfep_connection: F-feedback — the steering force depends on the gap between current and desired velocity. Close to the target, F diminishes. This is a self-regulating system: the closer you get, the gentler the approach. Negative feedback as navigation strategy.

exercise_1_8_solution_attraction_magnitu.capacity: FEEL that an orbit is a perpetual fall that always misses the ground — attraction creates structure from distance and direction
exercise_1_8_solution_attraction_magnitu.description: Inverse-square attraction. Closer means stronger. A ball orbits a grabbable attractor — drag it in VR and the orbit reshapes in real time. Elliptical paths emerge from the interplay of tangential velocity and radial pull. F = strength * dir / r-squared. An orbit is a perpetual fall that always misses the ground.
exercise_1_8_solution_attraction_magnitu.gamwell_reference: Classical mechanics, Newtonian dynamics, Nature of Code
interactions: grab attractor sphere in VR and drag
watch orbit reshape when attractor moves
exercise_1_8_solution_attraction_magnitu.name: Attraction and Orbit
exercise_1_8_solution_attraction_magnitu.qfep_connection: F as geometry — inverse-square means force IS a function of distance. The orbit shape encodes the relationship between speed and attraction. Move the attractor mid-orbit and watch deterministic chaos: same law, different trajectory.

hl_turret_vectors.description: Half-Life inspired sentry turret demonstrating ALL vector operations in one coherent system: subtraction (direction to target), magnitude (distance/range check), normalization (unit direction), dot product (FOV check), cross product (rotation axis), projection (ground plane), scalar multiplication (bullet velocity), and velocity integration (bullet physics). Fires tracer rounds with visible velocity vectors!
interactions: grab target sphere to move it
hl_turret_vectors.name: Half-Life Turret - Vector Compendium

parameters.show_bullet_vectors: Show velocity arrows on bullets (default true)

hl_turret_vectors.qfep_connection: The turret as computational subject - vectors as the mathematics of surveillance, targeting, and ballistics. Shows how abstract math operations have immediate, embodied applications in games and simulations.

laser_turret.description: Standalone laser turret that auto-targets and destroys balls. Place separately from ball_dropper to customize layout. Demonstrates vector subtraction (direction), magnitude (range), normalization (aim), dot product (lock).
interactions: Automatic targeting - no direct interaction needed
laser_turret.name: Laser Turret
laser_turret.qfep_connection: The turret as computational subject - continuously computing direction vectors to track moving targets.

sentry_turret.description: Half-Life style sentry turret. Targets balls and/or player. Simple reliable targeting with bullet physics. Emits signals for hits.
sentry_turret.name: Sentry Turret
sentry_turret.qfep_connection: The turret as autonomous agent - continuously computing vectors to track and engage targets.

sphere_splitting_showcase.description: sphere → fragments(method). Five fracture algorithms: planar cut, octree division, orange-peel sectors, CSG boolean, pre-segmented mesh. One sphere, five deaths.
sphere_splitting_showcase.name: sphere_splitting_showcase

turret_boll_infoboard.description: 3m × 6m semi-transparent infoboard showing ALL vector operations in one static diagram: subtraction (direction), magnitude (range), normalization (aim), dot product (lock), projection (prediction). Visual reference for turret targeting math.
turret_boll_infoboard.name: Turret-Boll Vector Diagram
turret_boll_infoboard.qfep_connection: The diagram as pedagogical synthesis - all vector operations unified through the targeting metaphor, showing how abstract math becomes embodied behavior.

turret_targeting.description: Combined turret + ball dropper setup. Laser turret tracks and destroys falling balls. Use laser_turret and ball_dropper separately for custom arrangements.
turret_targeting.name: Turret Targeting (Combined)

parameters.dropper_offset: Offset of ball dropper from turret (default 0,3,2)

turret_targeting.qfep_connection: Targeting as embodied vector math - the turret performs subtraction, normalization, and dot product continuously to track moving targets.

vector_addition_demo.description: Interactive vector addition visualizer: A + B = C. Shows parallelogram law with head-to-tail placement and ghost arrows.
interactions: grab handle spheres to adjust vectors
vector_addition_demo.name: Vector Addition
vector_addition_demo.qfep_connection: Composition - how separate movements combine into a single displacement

vector_addition_walk.description: Player-scale 3D vector addition. Walk inside a 3m coordinate grid, grab vector endpoints at body height, see parallelogram construction and component projections in real space.
interactions: grab handle spheres to adjust vectors A and B
walk through the grid to see components
vector_addition_walk.name: Vector Addition Walk (Room Scale)

parameters.grid_size: Size of walkable grid in meters (default 3.0)

vector_addition_walk.qfep_connection: Embodied composition: you ARE inside the vector space. Walk along X to feel the X component. Addition becomes spatial, not symbolic.

vector_drone.description: desired = (target - position).normalized() * speed. Chase, prepare, shoot, cooldown. A state machine driven by vector subtraction.
vector_drone.name: vector_drone

vector_field_visualizer.description: 3D arrow field showing flow — vortex, source, sink, or dipole fields. An 8x8x4 grid of arrow glyphs colored by magnitude (blue=slow, red=fast). Each arrow drawn with ImmediateMesh lines for shaft and arrowhead.
vector_field_visualizer.name: Vector Field Visualizer
vector_field_visualizer.qfep_connection: Vector fields as continuous flow — every point in space carries a direction, the field as a living topology of force and movement.

vector_joint_playground.description: Human-scale VR playground with 6 interactive stations. Each station pairs draggable vectors with a large physics joint mechanism: crane (magnitude), pistons (addition), door (dot product), seesaw (subtraction), waterwheel (cross product), spring tower (forces). Drag a vector, watch the machine respond.
interactions: read live math on info panels
vector_joint_playground.name: Vector-Joint Playground
vector_joint_playground.qfep_connection: Vectors as embodied forces — abstract math becomes physical machinery that moves, tilts, spins, and bounces at human scale

vector_magnitude_demo.description: Visualizes vector magnitude (length) using Pythagorean theorem. Shows |V| = √(x² + y² + z²).
vector_magnitude_demo.name: Vector Magnitude
vector_magnitude_demo.qfep_connection: Measurement - quantifying the 'amount' of a vector regardless of direction

vector_normalize_demo.description: Shows normalization: V̂ = V/|V|. Converts any vector to unit length while preserving direction.
vector_normalize_demo.name: Vector Normalization
vector_normalize_demo.qfep_connection: Pure direction - stripping magnitude to reveal only orientation

vector_projection_demo.description: Visualizes vector projection onto another vector or plane. Shows shadow/component decomposition.
vector_projection_demo.name: Vector Projection
vector_projection_demo.qfep_connection: Projection as filtering - extracting the component in a particular direction

vector_subtraction_demo.description: Interactive vector subtraction: A - B = C. Shows how subtraction finds the difference vector between two points.
vector_subtraction_demo.name: Vector Subtraction
vector_subtraction_demo.qfep_connection: Difference and direction - finding what separates two states

vector_translation_demo.description: Shows vectors as displacements in space. Position vectors and translation vectors.
vector_translation_demo.name: Vector Translation
vector_translation_demo.qfep_connection: Translation as movement - vectors as instructions for displacement

vectorpoint.description: Vector axes demonstration scene with grab sphere and info panel for 3D position breakdowns.
vectorpoint.name: VectorPoint

registry_info.description: Vector operation artifacts - addition, subtraction, magnitude, normalization, dot product, cross product, projection
registry_info.name: vectors
registry_info.theoretical_grounding: Linear algebra fundamentals, 3D graphics programming, physics simulation
